unmapped_findings: The paper does not report a discrete 500 °C/24 h data point specifically for the 4 wt.% Al alloy; the mechanical values available for 4Al are aggregated across aging conditions in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4.

b0025: The intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior.

b0031: For compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al (SIMPLEX steels) the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism; after aging at 500–600 °C twinning is reduced and strain hardening becomes associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening (relevant to this 4Al/500 °C aged sample).
No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations were found in the final RAP materials (b0021), and the 4 wt.% Al variant is reported as an intermediate variant between the 0Al and 8Al aging responses (b0024).
